 Prof. Sindhu R Pai

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Dictionary

Dictionary
•  Dictionary is a data structure that organizes data into key and value pairs
•  Every value has a certain unique key mapped to it
•   It is mutable (values can be changed after creation)


Dictionary Creation

>>> phonebook={} # Creation of empty dictionary
>>> phonebook={"Johan":938477565} # Dictionary with one key-value pair
>>> phonebook={"Johan":938477565,"Jill":938547565} # Dictionary with two key-value pair

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Dictionary

To access values in the dictionary, we use the keys like so:
>>> eng2french={ 1:’un’,
                     2:’deux’,
                        3:’trios’,
                     4:’quatre’,4: quatre ,
                    5:’cinq }
 >>> print(eng2french[2]) #will give you ‘deux’

Common operations on dictionaries

 Note: Dictionaries do not support ‘+’ and ‘*’ operations

Dictionary Functions

  •  get(): returns the value for a given key, if present.

  •  items(...)
           D.items() -> a set-like object providing a view on D’s items.

       D.pop(key) -> v, remove specified key and return the corresponding value. If
key is not found, otherwise KeyError is raised.

>>> print('person = ', person)

       D.setdefault(key,value) -> if the key is in the dictionary, returns its value. If the key
is not present, insert the key with a specified value and returns that same value.

>>> print('person = ',person)

Output:

phone = 90909090

Dictionary

       D.update() -> updates content of D with key-value pairs from a
        dictionary/iterable that it is given
>>> marks = {'Physics':67, 'Maths':87}
>>> internal_marks = {'Practical':48}
>>> marks.update( [(‘Chemistry’, 90), (‘Python’, 100)] )
>>> marks.update(internal_marks)
>>> print(marks)
